l4_steps.name: Extract aircraft maintenance due-date forecast
l4_steps.input: Aircraft flight hours, cycles, and calendar days from ACARS/flight ops feeds
l4_steps.output: Due-date forecast report showing C/D check windows per tail number
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast horizon ≥12 months; 100% of fleet tails covered
l4_steps.pain_point: CAMP data sync lag from ACARS can understate actual FH/FC by 1-2 cycles, risking check due-date miscalculation

l4_steps.name: Review AD/SB compliance status per tail
l4_steps.input: FAA Airworthiness Directives feed, manufacturer Service Bulletins, CAMP compliance tracker
l4_steps.output: AD/SB compliance gap list with mandated incorporation deadlines
l4_steps.kpi: Zero open mandatory ADs at check induction; SB review complete ≥90 days pre-induction
l4_steps.pain_point: Rapid-fire AD releases (e.g. Boeing MAX ADs post-737 MAX groundings) can invalidate a pre-built work scope days before induction

l4_steps.name: Determine check type: C-check vs D-check
l4_steps.input: Aircraft age, total flight cycles, last heavy check date, AD requirements
l4_steps.output: Confirmed check type decision (C1/C2/C3 or D-check) entered in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: Check type confirmed ≥9 months prior to induction date
l4_steps.pain_point: Legacy aircraft approaching D-check thresholds (typically 8-12 years) may be upgraded mid-plan; late D-check designation inflates TAT and cost >40%

l4_steps.name: Generate MPD baseline work package in AMOS
l4_steps.input: Approved check type, aircraft MPD (Boeing Maintenance Planning Document), AMOS task library
l4_steps.output: Baseline work package with task cards, intervals, and estimated manhours
l4_steps.kpi: Baseline work package issued ≥8 months prior to induction; manhour estimate accuracy ±10%
l4_steps.pain_point: MPD revision cycles from Boeing (quarterly) can introduce new tasks after baseline is locked, requiring rework of the work package

l4_steps.name: Incorporate deferred defects and open MEL items
l4_steps.input: Deferred defect register, MEL (Minimum Equipment List) open items from line maintenance logs
l4_steps.output: Updated work package with deferred items assigned to check package
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of Category A/B MEL items resolved at or before heavy check; deferred defect backlog cleared
l4_steps.pain_point: MEL items deferred beyond permissible intervals can trigger unplanned component removals, extending TAT by 3-5 days

l4_steps.name: Add Engineering Orders and requested modifications
l4_steps.input: Engineering Orders (EOs), STC modifications, cabin reconfiguration requests from fleet planning
l4_steps.output: Supplemental work scope with EOs and mods task-carded in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: All approved EOs incorporated ≥6 months pre-induction; no scope additions within 60 days of induction
l4_steps.pain_point: Cabin modification requests (seat layout changes, IFE upgrades) arriving late can increase ground time by 5-10 days and require renegotiation of MRO slot

l4_steps.name: Validate work scope against C-check threshold
l4_steps.input: Completed work scope package, manhour estimates, EO add-ons
l4_steps.output: Scope classification confirmed: C-check or escalated to D-check in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: Scope re-classification decisions completed within 5 business days of scope freeze; re-scope rate <5% of planned checks
l4_steps.pain_point: Scope creep during D-check escalation is poorly controlled — cumulative EOs can push TAT from 21 days to 45 days without formal gate review

l4_steps.name: Estimate total manhours and skill requirements
l4_steps.input: Approved work scope package with task cards
l4_steps.output: Manhour demand plan broken down by trade (structures, avionics, engines, interiors)
l4_steps.kpi: Manhour forecast accuracy ±15% vs actuals; plan issued ≥6 months pre-induction
l4_steps.pain_point: Structures trade skill shortages at third-party MROs (particularly composite repair) can stretch avail windows; market-rate labour cost escalation unpredictable >6 months out

l4_steps.name: Identify and order long-lead rotable parts
l4_steps.input: AMOS work package BOM, CAMP part cross-reference, current inventory positions
l4_steps.output: Long-lead parts list with order quantities, lead times, and due-in dates
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of long-lead parts (lead time >90 days) on order ≥6 months pre-induction; stockout rate at induction <2%
l4_steps.pain_point: Boeing 737 MAX supply chain disruptions (e.g. Spirit AeroSystems fuselage quality holds 2024) can delay rotable availability by 4-8 weeks, forcing work scope deferral

l4_steps.name: Raise material requisitions for consumables and hardware
l4_steps.input: AMOS-generated materials list, approved vendor catalogue in SAP Ariba
l4_steps.output: Purchase requisitions raised and approved in SAP Ariba; delivery schedule confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: All consumable PRs raised ≥90 days pre-induction; on-time delivery rate ≥95%
l4_steps.pain_point: Spot-buy requirements for unplanned findings inflate procurement cost by 20-40%; Ariba spot-buy approvals can take 5-10 days, delaying line opening

l4_steps.name: Confirm critical parts availability at MRO site
l4_steps.input: SAP Ariba purchase orders, MRO facility inventory feed, Boeing Toolbox part status
l4_steps.output: Parts readiness confirmation report; open shortages escalated
l4_steps.kpi: Parts readiness confirmation completed 30 days pre-induction; critical shortage count = 0 at induction
l4_steps.pain_point: MRO-to-airline inventory visibility gaps mean shortages are discovered at induction rather than pre-induction, causing AOG-equivalent delays mid-check

l4_steps.name: Issue RFQ to approved heavy MRO facilities
l4_steps.input: Approved work scope package, manhour estimates, parts supply plan, desired induction window
l4_steps.output: RFQ document issued to ≥3 qualified MRO vendors via SAP Ariba sourcing event
l4_steps.kpi: RFQ issued ≥9 months pre-induction; minimum 3 qualified vendor responses received
l4_steps.pain_point: Global MRO capacity constraints (post-pandemic backlog) reduce competitive vendor responses; sole-source situations remove cost leverage and inflate quotes by 15-30%

l4_steps.name: Evaluate vendor bids on TAT, cost, and capability
l4_steps.input: Vendor bids, MRO capability audit records, historical TAT performance data
l4_steps.output: Bid evaluation scorecard with vendor ranking; recommendation memo
l4_steps.kpi: Evaluation complete within 15 business days of bid close; cost variance between lowest and selected bid <8%
l4_steps.pain_point: MRO vendors routinely under-quote TAT to win contract then invoke 'findings escalation' clauses — actual TAT can exceed quoted by 20-35%, disrupting aircraft utilisation plan

l4_steps.name: Confirm bid meets TAT and unit cost targets
l4_steps.input: Bid evaluation scorecard, fleet plan TAT requirements, approved MRO budget
l4_steps.output: Approved vendor selection or instruction to re-issue RFQ / negotiate
l4_steps.kpi: Contract TAT ≤21 days for C-check, ≤45 days for D-check; unit cost within ±5% of approved budget
l4_steps.pain_point: Approval delays at VP level (budget cycles, contract committee scheduling) can compress negotiation window, forcing acceptance of sub-optimal bids

l4_steps.name: Award contract and raise PO in SAP
l4_steps.input: Approved vendor selection, agreed contract terms, budget approval
l4_steps.output: Signed MRO contract, purchase order raised in SAP S/4HANA, cost centre committed
l4_steps.kpi: PO raised within 5 business days of approval; contract signed ≥6 months pre-induction
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP Ariba–to–S/4HANA PO hand-off failures (integration errors) can delay cost commitment, blocking parts release and hangar slot confirmation

l4_steps.name: Compile aircraft technical documentation package
l4_steps.input: Aircraft log books, CAMP airworthiness records, work scope package, AD/SB status report
l4_steps.output: Complete pre-induction documentation pack transmitted to MRO facility
l4_steps.kpi: Documentation package delivered to MRO ≥14 days before induction; zero missing mandatory documents at induction gate
l4_steps.pain_point: Paper-based or siloed digital records from legacy line maintenance systems create gaps in technical records; missing logbook entries can halt induction pending FAA review

l4_steps.name: Coordinate ferry flight and fleet schedule impact
l4_steps.input: Confirmed MRO induction date, aircraft tail assignment, fleet plan from SkyWORKS
l4_steps.output: Ferry flight plan, substitute aircraft allocation, schedule change notification to OCC
l4_steps.kpi: Ferry flight confirmed ≥21 days pre-induction; schedule impact to revenue flying <2 affected rotations
l4_steps.pain_point: Last-minute fleet reassignments to cover operational disruptions can pull the designated heavy-check aircraft back into service, delaying induction and incurring MRO slot-break fees

l4_steps.name: Complete pre-induction readiness checklist
l4_steps.input: Documentation pack status, parts delivery confirmations, ferry flight plan, MRO slot confirmation
l4_steps.output: Signed pre-induction checklist; go/no-go decision for induction
l4_steps.kpi: Checklist signed-off 7 days pre-induction; no-go rate due to planning gaps <3%
l4_steps.pain_point: No-go decisions within 7 days of induction trigger MRO penalty fees (typically $15-25K/day for slot breaks) and ripple delay to subsequent planned checks
